purpose: Regression tripwire for the blocker fixed in db6cd81d. Every route listed here rendered real published content on 2026-09-10 and is expected to keep doing so. NF17 compares the live census against this file. It is NOT F24's gate — A19 (disclosure) is. It exists because every other assertion in contract-f24.yaml stays GREEN if all six silently revert to disclosed shells: the fallback machinery would be verified working while the thing it substitutes for had vanished.
establishedBy: db6cd81d — fix(nos): hyphenate seed document ids — unblocks the six 404ing show routes

verdicts.PASS: Every route in expectedPublished renders `published`, and the set of published routes matches this file exactly.
verdicts.FAIL: THE TRIPWIRE FIRED. A route in expectedPublished rendered `fallback-unpublished`. Its content regressed — check the named seed and the seeding run before anything else. This is the db6cd81d blocker returning.
verdicts.DRIFT: The live set and this file disagree in a way that is not a regression: a route renders `published` that is not listed here, or a route listed here is no longer a listed:true row in the manifest. Someone added or retired a page without recording it. THE FIX IS TO EDIT THIS FILE in the same commit that made the change — not to loosen the check.

howToRetireAPage: Remove its entry here, in the same commit that retires the route. The edit is the record: it has an author, a diff and a commit message, which a gate colour does not. Never widen the check to make a retirement pass silently.
notes: DRIFT is deliberately a distinct verdict token, not folded into FAIL, so a legitimate retirement is legible at a glance instead of arriving as a mysterious red.
This file is a baseline, never a count. An assertion written as `published == 6` cannot tell a broken seed from a deliberately retired page; both look like the same red.
13-booking-tickets.json is seeded but backs no listed:true route, so it is deliberately absent from expectedPublished.
